items.title: Mount the root filesystem read-only
items.rationale: Writable root filesystems make persistence and tampering easier after compromise.
actions: Move writable paths to explicit emptyDir or persistent volumes.
Validate startup scripts and temp directories still work after the change.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: REPLACE_ME
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cua
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: REPLACE_ME
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          runAsGroup: 10001
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault

items.title: Reduce service account token exposure
items.rationale: Mounted service account tokens expand blast radius when a pod is compromised and should be disabled unless the workload truly needs Kubernetes API access.
actions: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false for workloads that do not need the API.
Use a dedicated least-privilege service account when API access is required.
Keep token mounts read-only and review RBAC bindings.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sandbox-sa
  namespace: default
automountServiceAccountToken: false

items.title: Remove setuid/setgid binaries from the image
items.rationale: Setuid and setgid binaries create extra privilege-escalation paths even when the container is otherwise hardened.
actions: Remove unnecessary setuid/setgid binaries from the image.
Prefer distroless or minimal base images where possible.
Verify no operational tooling depends on privilege-granting helpers.
items.snippet: Rebuild the image without unnecessary setuid/setgid helpers.

templates.network_policy:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: sandbox-default-deny
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cua
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
  ingress: []
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector: {}
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          k8s-app: kube-dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 53
templates.service_account:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sandbox-sa
  namespace: default
automountServiceAccountToken: false
templates.kyverno_policy:
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: sandbox-restricted
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  rules:
  - name: require-restricted-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: Enforce restricted securityContext for sandbox workloads.
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              seccompProfile:
                type: RuntimeDefault
templates.gatekeeper_template:
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredSandboxSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "Sandbox pods must set readOnlyRootFilesystem=true"
      }

ai_advisor.executive_summary: Three issues raise a high-risk score for the Deployment target-cua: exposed service account tokens, writable root filesystem, and setuid/setgid binaries in the image. All fixes require manual design or image changes and cannot be auto-applied.
ai_advisor.remediation_overview: Prioritize eliminating credentials exposure and minimizing runtime privileges. Implement workload and image changes: remove or limit service account token mounts, enforce read-only rootfs with explicit writable volumes, and rebuild images without setuid/setgid binaries. Validate each change in a staging environment before production roll-out.

prioritized_groups.title: Credentials & API access
prioritized_groups.rationale: Service account tokens enable cluster API access and have highest blast/probability contribution.

prioritized_groups.title: Runtime filesystem immutability
prioritized_groups.rationale: Writable root increases persistence and lateral movement risk; mitigations require app validation.

prioritized_groups.title: Image hardening
prioritized_groups.rationale: Setuid/setgid binaries increase privilege escalation risk; fix via image rebuild.

item_advice.explanation: Pod has access to a mounted service account token, allowing in-cluster API access if not needed.
item_advice.operator_impact: May break code that relies on Kubernetes API or in-cluster credentials; requires code or RBAC changes.
item_advice.validation_advice: Deploy to staging with tokens removed (projected tokens or no token) and test all API calls and credential flows.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Removing token exposure reduces highest-risk attack vector and should be addressed first.

item_advice.explanation: Container root filesystem is writable, enabling runtime tampering and persistence.
item_advice.operator_impact: Applications that write to root paths will fail; verify writable paths and provide writable volumes (/tmp, workspace).
item_advice.validation_advice: Enable readOnlyRootFilesystem in a test rollout, mount required writable emptyDir volumes, and run full functional tests.
item_advice.ordering_reason: After tokens, enforcing read-only root limits attacker persistence and complements least-privilege controls.

item_advice.explanation: Image contains setuid/setgid binaries which attackers can abuse for privilege escalation.
item_advice.operator_impact: Requires image rebuild or upstream image change; may affect functionality if legitimate setuid is required.
item_advice.validation_advice: Rebuild image without setuid/setgid files, run application integration and security scans, and compare behavior in staging.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Image hardening is lower immediate blast than tokens/rootfs but should follow to reduce escalation paths.

ai_advisor.guided_operator_message: Address service account token exposure and read-only rootfs first in staging; then rebuild images to remove setuid/setgid binaries. Validate each step before production.
warnings: Do not apply changes directly in production without staging validation.
Removing tokens or enabling read-only root may break legitimate application behavior.
Image changes may require CI/CD and dependency updates.
next_steps: Confirm whether workload needs Kubernetes API access; if not, disable service account tokens or use minimal projected tokens.
Identify application write paths and configure writable volumes; enable readOnlyRootFilesystem in staging.
Locate and remove setuid/setgid binaries from base image; rebuild and test images.
Run full integration and security tests in staging before rolling changes to production.
